region.text: Sylhet, the northern plains of the bridge

ledger.note: 1612: Sylhet leaves the 1490 bridge. Sylhet page: "In the 16th century, Sylhet was controlled by the Baro-Bhuiyan zamindars" and "Sylhet emerged after 1612 as the Mughals' most significant imperial outpost in Bengal east of Dhaka"; "Later it became a sarkar (district) of the Mughal Empire". The page names no Tripura loss and no month, so the date is the Mughal outpost's; the Manikya dynasty page has Tripura "brought under Mughal suzerainty in the early 17th century". Mirror: mughal-empire keyframes 1612-1669 add the Sylhet disc (an event there would renumber that ledger, which other files cite). Review fx-10 (1 Nov 2026): confidence lowered from 2 to 1, because the same Sylhet page puts Sylhet under 'the Baro-Bhuiyan zamindars' in the 16th century, so Tripura's hold until 1612 is only the end of the 1490 bridge, not a dated loss.

1666: the port of Chittagong, inside the bridge's Chittagong Hill Tracts disc, becomes Mughal. History of Chittagong page: "The Mughal Army defeated the Arakanese Army and successfully annexed Chatgaon to the Mughal Empire in 1666"; before that the page has the Bengal Sultanate, Arakan and the Portuguese in Chittagong, with Tripura only in 'parts of modern Chittagong' under Dhanya Manikya. The Hill Tracts proper are not said to have been Mughal and stay in the bridge until ledger loss 1764 (no opened page dates their loss, so that date is not moved).

region.text: the plains of the kingdom: Comilla, Noakhali, Sylhet

ledger.note: 1733: 'Mughal dominance of the plains of the kingdom'. A client kingdom is not the Mughals' own land, but the plains leave the Manikya kings' rule (the hills stay independent), so the loss is drawn as a transfer to the Mughal side; the Chittagong Hill Tracts, listed among the kingdom's lands at its height, are not named by the page here.

minus.text: Tripura: the hill kingdom of the Manikya kings (the princely state of Hill Tippera)

ledger.note: 1764: 'when the British East India Company took control of Bengal' the Mughal-held parts of Bengal passed to British administration; the page does not mention Tripura's lowlands again, and the kings kept only the Chakla Roshnabad estate (1,476 km2), a landlord's holding rather than a state's land. The Chittagong Hill Tracts go as a bridge: the 1941 area of 10,660 km2 leaves no room for them in the princely state, but no page opened says when they were lost; the year is the Company's.
1905: Tripura 'joined Eastern Bengal and Assam as Hill Tippera'. The page gives the name for the princely state; the border does not change.

region.text: Tripura: the hill kingdom of the Manikya kings (the princely state of Hill Tippera)

ledger.note: 15 October 1949: the state merges into the Union of India as a Part C State (the Tripura Merger Agreement was signed on 9 September 1949; the infobox has the merger on 15 October). Kirit Bikram Kishore, a minor, was the last ruler (1947-1949).

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, four new keyframes. Four pages opened (Kingdom of Tripura, Tripura (princely state), History of Tripura, Tripura); the Company rule in India page (opened earlier in this run for east-india-company) supplies the 1858 hand-over. Chakla Roshanabad failed (url_not_found). WebFetch returned extracts.

Thin evidence: the pages date almost none of the kingdom's territorial changes. Dated: the infobox span (c. 1400 to 15 October 1949), Maha Manikya's accession (1400), Dhanya Manikya's reign (1463-1515 on the Kingdom page, 1490-1515 on the History page), the Koch capture of the Barak Valley (1562), Mughal dominance of the plains (1733), the Company's control of Bengal (1764), the protectorate (1809), recognition as sovereigns (1838), the accession (13 August 1947) and the merger (9 September agreement, 15 October 1949). Not dated: Sylhet, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the Eastern Bengal plains at the kingdom's height (drawn as one bridged gain at 1490, confidence 1), the Hailakandi valley (annexed by a Kachari king in the 18th century), the capital moves.

Handling of the suzerainties: vassal_start and vassal_end belong to the suzerain's dossier (counterpart = the vassal), so the Mughal client status of the plains (1733), the 1809 protectorate, the Crown's from 1858 and the accession of 13 August 1947 are listed at the end of these notes for the suzerain's dossier, and east-india-company records the 1809 protectorate. The lowland plains are drawn as lost to the Mughal side in 1733 (confidence 2) and the Chittagong Hill Tracts as lost to the Company in 1764 (confidence 1, a bridge from the 1941 area).

Not drawn: the Chakla Roshnabad estate (1,476 km2, in Noakhali, Sylhet and Tipperah; kept by the kings as landlords after the Company took the plains), the Kuki raids of 1826-1862, and the Bengal Sultanate wars (the pages date none). The 1941 princely-state area (10,660 km2) is a little larger than the modern Tripura admin-1 on the grid (about 9,600 km2). No ruler strip: the princely-state page lists reigns only from 1684 and 'selected'.

Cross-dossier: koch-bihar (counterpart of the 1562 loss, written by this batch), mughal-empire, east-india-company, british-raj, republic-of-india. Gazetteer: Noakhali is absent (91.10 E 22.87 N, 35 km used), as is the Barak Valley (centre 92.65 E 24.75 N, 60 km) and the Chittagong Hill Tracts (92.2 E 22.5 N, 55 km).

Suzerainty events kept out of the ledger: vassal_start and vassal_end belong in the suzerain's dossier with this state as the counterpart (the schema: 'counterpart is the vassal itself'), so they are listed here for whoever writes or checks the suzerain. 1733 vassal_start (suzerain mughal-empire, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripura): 1733: the struggle for the throne 'culminated in Mughal dominance of the plains of the kingdom in 1733'; the Kingdom page says the plains became a Mughal client kingdom after a renegade prince was backed by Mughal governors. Drawn for the lowland circles only; the hills stayed independent. | 1809 vassal_start (suzerain east-india-company, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripura_(princely_state)): 1809: 'Tripura became a British protectorate' (a subsidiary alliance that lasted until the Indian Independence Act 1947). | 1858-11 vassal_end (suzerain east-india-company, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India): 1 November 1858: the Company's protected states pass to the Crown with the rest of its rights (Company rule page); the Tripura pages give no separate act. | 1858-11 vassal_start (suzerain british-raj, confidence 2, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India): 1 November 1858: the Crown takes over the protectorate (see the previous entry). The princely-state page adds that 'in 1838 the Rajas of Tripura were recognised by the British as sovereigns' and that in 1871 a British agent was appointed. | 1947-08 vassal_end (suzerain british-raj, confidence 3, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripura_(princely_state)): 13 August 1947: the infobox gives the accession to India; the subsidiary alliance was released by the Indian Independence Act 1947. The page gives no separate date for the lapse of paramountcy.
